facts.name: Death Benefit Amount

facts.name: Death Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: The death benefit is payable upon the insured's death while the policy is in force.

facts.name: Death Benefit Time Limit
facts.sentence: The death benefit is subject to the condition that death occurs before November 18, 2034.

facts.name: Proof of Death Requirement
facts.sentence: Satisfactory proof of death must be received by the insurer to trigger the death benefit payout.

facts.name: Cause of Death Exclusion Condition
facts.sentence: The cause of death must not be excluded under section 8 for the death benefit to be paid.

facts.name: Table Rating Definition
facts.sentence: A table rating reflects the insured's elevated risk profile.

facts.name: Table Rating Percentage Basis
facts.sentence: A table rating is expressed as a percentage addition to standard rates.

facts.name: Table A Standard Risk
facts.sentence: Table A corresponds to standard risk and incurs no additional rate increase.

facts.name: Table Rating Increase
facts.sentence: Each subsequent table increases the premium by approximately 25% over standard rates.

facts.name: Table D Risk Surcharge
facts.sentence: Table D (4) represents a 100% increase above standard rates.

facts.name: Flat Extra Premium Definition
facts.sentence: The flat extra premium is an additional per-thousand charge applied for a defined period.

facts.name: Flat Extra Premium Purpose
facts.sentence: The flat extra premium accounts for a specific identified risk, namely occupational hazard.

facts.name: Temporary Flat Extra Premium
facts.sentence: The flat extra premium is temporary and ends after year 5.

facts.name: Grace Period Duration
facts.sentence: The grace period is 31 days following each missed monthly premium due date.

facts.name: Occupational Hazard During Flat Extra
facts.sentence: The occupational hazard exclusion applies during the flat extra period.

facts.name: Occupational Hazard Exclusion
facts.sentence: Section 8.2 describes the occupational hazard exclusion.

facts.name: Lump Sum Death Benefit
facts.sentence: The death benefit is paid in a lump sum.

facts.name: Death Benefit Payout Timeline
facts.sentence: The death benefit is paid within 30 days of claim approval.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Within Two Years
facts.sentence: Section 8 excludes deaths caused by suicide within two years of the issue date.

facts.name: Suicide Clause Liability Limit
facts.sentence: If the insured dies by suicide within two years of the issue date, the insurer's liability is limited to a refund of premiums paid.

facts.name: Flat Extra Expiration
facts.sentence: The occupational flat extra of $200.00 per month expires at the end of policy year 5.

facts.name: Flat Extra Expiration Date
facts.sentence: The occupational flat extra of $200.00 per month expires on November 18, 2029.

facts.name: Automatic Expiry Adjustment
facts.sentence: No notification or action by the owner is required when the occupational flat extra expires.

facts.name: Premium Reduction After Flat Extra Expiry
facts.sentence: The monthly premium automatically reduces to $268.13 per month after the flat extra expires.

facts.name: Reduced Premium Effective Date
facts.sentence: The reduced monthly premium begins with the premium due on December 18, 2029.

facts.name: Re-evaluation Request Right
facts.sentence: The owner may request a re-evaluation of the occupational hazard surcharge at any time during the flat extra period.

facts.name: Occupation Change & Surcharge Review
facts.sentence: A change in occupation may trigger a request for re-evaluation of the occupational hazard surcharge.

facts.name: Occupation Change Re-Evaluation Requirement
facts.sentence: Written evidence of a change in occupation must be submitted to initiate a re-evaluation.

facts.name: Insurer Discretion on Surcharge Review
facts.sentence: Re-evaluation of the occupational hazard surcharge is at the insurer’s sole discretion.

facts.name: Monthly Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: The monthly premium is due on the 18th of each month.

facts.name: Grace Period for Premium Payments
facts.sentence: A grace period of 31 days follows each missed premium due date.

facts.name: Premium Lapse After Grace Period
facts.sentence: Non-payment of the premium after the grace period results in policy lapse.

facts.name: Policy Reinstatement Window
facts.sentence: Reinstatement is available within 2 years of lapse.

facts.name: Reinstatement Insurability Requirement
facts.sentence: Evidence of insurability satisfactory to the insurer is required for reinstatement.

facts.name: Reinstatement Premium Interest
facts.sentence: Overdue premiums must be paid with 7% interest for reinstatement.

facts.name: Reinstatement Requires Revised Terms
facts.sentence: Any revised rating terms must be accepted for reinstatement.

facts.name: Diabetes Exclusion Liability Limit
facts.sentence: Our liability is limited to a refund of premiums paid if a claim occurs within two years of the issue date.

facts.name: Commercial Diving Exclusion (Years 1–5)
facts.sentence: During policy years 1 through 5, no death benefit is payable if death results directly from the insured's performance of commercial diving operations.

facts.name: Saturation Diving Exclusion
facts.sentence: Commercial diving operations include saturation diving.

facts.name: Mixed Gas Diving Exclusion
facts.sentence: Commercial diving operations include mixed gas diving.

facts.name: Surface-Supplied Diving Exclusion
facts.sentence: Commercial diving operations include surface-supplied diving.

facts.name: Commercial Diving Exclusion
facts.sentence: Commercial diving operations include underwater construction activities.

facts.name: Commercial Diving Exclusion Scope
facts.sentence: Commercial diving operations include underwater inspection activities.

facts.name: Underwater Salvage Exclusion
facts.sentence: Commercial diving operations include underwater salvage activities.

facts.name: Occupational Diving Definition
facts.sentence: Commercial diving operations include any diving activity performed in an occupational capacity.

facts.name: Commercial Diving Refund Clause
facts.sentence: If death results directly from commercial diving during policy years 1 through 5, premiums paid will be refunded with 4% annual interest.

facts.name: Post-Year-5 Exclusion Termination
facts.sentence: After policy year 5, the occupational hazard exclusion terminates.

facts.name: Post-Year-5 Diving Coverage
facts.sentence: After policy year 5, death resulting from any commercial diving activity is fully covered by the death benefit.

facts.name: Diabetes Therapy Noncompliance Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the insured fails to maintain insulin therapy as prescribed.

facts.name: Diabetes Medication Noncompliance Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the insured fails to maintain medication therapy as prescribed.

facts.name: Diabetes Complication Exclusion
facts.sentence: Death resulting directly from uncontrolled diabetic ketoacidosis within the first two policy years triggers the diabetes complication exclusion.

facts.name: Diabetes Exclusion Trigger
facts.sentence: Death resulting directly from hyperosmolar hyperglycemic crisis within the first two policy years triggers the diabetes complication exclusion.

facts.name: Diabetes Exclusion Time Limit
facts.sentence: The diabetes complication exclusion applies only within the first two policy years.

facts.name: Exclusions Limitation Statement
facts.sentence: No other exclusions apply beyond those specified in Sections 8.2, 8.3, and 8.4.

facts.name: Rating Review Eligibility
facts.sentence: The policy owner may request a formal review of the Table D rating on or after the third policy anniversary.

facts.name: Rating Review Requirement
facts.sentence: A rating review requires a written request from the policy owner.

facts.name: Rating Review Requirement
facts.sentence: A rating review requires a current attending physician’s statement.

facts.name: Rating Review Requirements
facts.sentence: A rating review requires HbA1c laboratory results dated within 90 days.

facts.name: Rating Review Fee Requirement
facts.sentence: A rating review requires payment of a $150.00 review fee.

facts.name: Rating Review Outcome
facts.sentence: If a rating review supports a reduction in mortality risk, the insurer may reduce the table rating.

facts.name: Prospective Premium Adjustment
facts.sentence: Any adjustment to the premium due to a rating review takes effect prospectively.

facts.name: No Retroactive Premium Refund
facts.sentence: No premium refund is available for periods before the effective date of any rating improvement.

facts.name: Rating Review Frequency Limit
facts.sentence: The insurer may decline to conduct a rating review more than once per policy year.

facts.name: No Conversion Privilege
facts.sentence: This substandard-rated policy does not include a conversion privilege to a permanent policy on a guaranteed basis.

facts.name: Substandard Policy Rating
facts.sentence: This policy is rated as substandard.

facts.name: No Guaranteed Conversion Privilege
facts.sentence: This substandard-rated policy does not include a conversion privilege to a permanent policy on a guaranteed basis.

facts.name: Term Renewal Option
facts.sentence: An insured person may apply for a new individual policy at the expiry of this term.

facts.name: Post-Term Policy Renewal Underwriting
facts.sentence: Any application for a new individual policy at the expiry of this term is subject to full underwriting at the time of application.

facts.name: Death Claim Submission Requirement
facts.sentence: To file a death claim, Form RL-CLM-01 must be submitted.

facts.name: Death Claim Documentation Requirement
facts.sentence: To file a death claim, a certified copy of the death certificate must be submitted.

facts.name: Death Claim Documentation Requirement
facts.sentence: To file a death claim, an attending physician's statement indicating cause of death must be submitted.

facts.name: Diving Logs Requirement
facts.sentence: If the claim arises due to occupation-related activity, diving logs must be submitted for claims occurring during policy years 1–5.

facts.name: Occupational Claim Documentation Requirement
facts.sentence: If the claim arises due to occupation-related activity, employer records must be submitted for claims occurring during policy years 1–5.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: All required documents for a death claim must be submitted to Resolute Life & Risk Insurance Company.

facts.name: Claim Submission Location
facts.sentence: All required documents for a death claim must be submitted to the Specialty Risk Claims Unit.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: All required documents for a death claim must be sent to 2500 Risk Management Plaza, Dallas, TX 75201.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Resolute Life & Risk Insurance Company will pay valid claims within 30 days of receiving all required documentation.

facts.name: Incontestability Clause
facts.sentence: After two years from the issue date, Resolute Life & Risk Insurance Company may not contest this policy based on misrepresentation.

facts.name: Non-Payment Contestability
facts.sentence: Non-payment of premium remains a valid reason for contesting the policy even after two years from the issue date.

facts.name: Diabetes Exclusion Exception
facts.sentence: The diabetes exclusion specified in Section 8 is not subject to the incontestability clause.

facts.name: Occupational Exclusion Exception
facts.sentence: The occupational exclusion specified in Section 8 is not subject to the incontestability clause.

facts.name: Misstatement of Age or Sex Adjustment
facts.sentence: If the age or sex of the insured is misstated, benefits will be adjusted to reflect the amount that could have been purchased at the correct age and sex.

facts.name: Benefits Adjustment for Misstatement
facts.sentence: Benefits adjustment due to misstatement of age or sex occurs under the applicable rating class.

facts.name: Entire Contract Clause
facts.sentence: This policy and the application together constitute the entire contract between the parties.

facts.name: Governing Law Jurisdiction
facts.sentence: This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Texas.

facts.name: Issuing Entity Identification
facts.sentence: Resolute Life & Risk Insurance Company is the issuing entity of the document.

facts.name: Chief Underwriting Officer Authorization
facts.sentence: The position responsible for authorization on the document is Chief Underwriting Officer — Specialty Risk.

facts.name: Document Issue Date
facts.sentence: The document was issued on November 18, 2024.

facts.name: Signature Line Presence
facts.sentence: An authorized signature line appears on the document.

facts.name: Signature Placement
facts.sentence: The signature line is located beneath the title 'Chief Underwriting Officer — Specialty Risk'.

facts.name: Policy Number Identification
facts.sentence: The policy number is BP-2024-ROP-00441.

facts.name: Policy Issue Date
facts.sentence: The issue date of the policy is February 1, 2024.

facts.name: 25-Year ROP Term Policy
facts.sentence: The policy type is 25-Year Return-of-Premium Level Term Life Insurance.

facts.name: Policy Owner Identity
facts.sentence: The policy owner is Diane Marie Kowalski.

facts.name: Insured Person Identified
facts.sentence: The insured person is Diane Marie Kowalski.

facts.name: Insured Person’s Date of Birth
facts.sentence: The date of birth of the insured person is July 9, 1982.

facts.name: Insured Age at Issue
facts.sentence: The age of the insured person at issue is 41 years.

facts.name: Preferred Risk Classification
facts.sentence: The risk class of the insured person is Preferred Non-Tobacco.

facts.name: Death Benefit Amount
facts.sentence: The death benefit amount is $750,000.

facts.name: Level Death Benefit
facts.sentence: The death benefit is level throughout the term of the policy.

facts.name: Policy Term Duration
facts.sentence: The policy term is 25 years.

facts.name: Policy Expiration Date
facts.sentence: The policy expires on February 1, 2049.

facts.name: Monthly Base Premium
facts.sentence: The base premium is $118.00 per month.

facts.name: Monthly Automatic Deduction
facts.sentence: The premium payment mode is monthly automatic deduction.

facts.name: Return-of-Premium Date
facts.sentence: The return-of-premium date is February 1, 2049.

facts.name: Return-of-Premium Maturity Alignment
facts.sentence: The return-of-premium date corresponds to the policy maturity date.

facts.name: Primary Beneficiary Designation
facts.sentence: The primary beneficiary is Thomas Alan Kowalski.

facts.name: Spousal Beneficiary Designation
facts.sentence: Thomas Alan Kowalski is designated as the spouse of the insured person.

facts.name: Primary Beneficiary Payout
facts.sentence: The primary beneficiary receives 100% of the death benefit.

facts.name: Contingent Beneficiary Designation
facts.sentence: The contingent beneficiary is the Kowalski Family Trust.

facts.name: Kowalski Family Trust Establishment
facts.sentence: The Kowalski Family Trust was established on January 10, 2023.

facts.name: Contingent Beneficiary Payout Rule
facts.sentence: The contingent beneficiary receives 100% of the death benefit if the primary beneficiary predeceases the insured person.

facts.name: Definition of Death Benefit
facts.sentence: Section 4.1 defines 'Death Benefit' as the face amount payable upon the insured's death while the policy is in force.

facts.name: Return-of-Premium Definition
facts.sentence: Section 4.2 defines 'Return-of-Premium Benefit' (ROP) as the total of all base premiums paid.

facts.name: Death Benefit Definition
facts.sentence: Death Benefit means the face amount payable upon the insured's death while this policy is in force.

facts.name: Death Benefit Claim Condition
facts.sentence: We will pay the death benefit to the named beneficiary upon receipt of satisfactory proof of the insured's death.

facts.name: Death Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: We will pay the death benefit to the named beneficiary upon death occurring while this policy is in force.

facts.name: Death Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: We will pay the death benefit to the named beneficiary upon death occurring before the policy maturity date.

facts.name: Lump Sum Death Benefit Payout
facts.sentence: Payment of the death benefit shall be made in a single lump sum within 30 days of approval of a complete claim submission.

facts.name: Grace Period Deduction Rule
facts.sentence: If the insured dies during the grace period before the overdue premium is paid, we will deduct any unpaid premium from the death benefit before payment.

facts.name: Return-of-Premium Benefit Definition
facts.sentence: Return-of-Premium Benefit (ROP) means the total of all base premiums paid to us under this policy, returned to the owner if the insured survives to the policy maturity date.

facts.name: Policy Maturity Date Definition
facts.sentence: Policy Maturity Date means February 1, 2049.

facts.name: Return-of-Premium Eligibility
facts.sentence: If the insured is living on the policy maturity date and this policy has not lapsed, we will pay the owner a return-of-premium benefit equal to the sum of all base premiums actually paid under this policy.

facts.name: ROP Excludes Optional Riders
facts.sentence: The Return-of-Premium Benefit does not include premiums for optional riders.

facts.name: ROP Excludes Reinstatement Fees
facts.sentence: The Return-of-Premium Benefit does not include reinstatement fees.

facts.name: ROP Excludes Wellness Credits
facts.sentence: The Return-of-Premium Benefit does not include any Wellness Credits received.

facts.name: ROP Benefit Termination
facts.sentence: Payment of the Return-of-Premium Benefit terminates this policy.

facts.name: ROP Not Payable on Assignment
facts.sentence: The Return-of-Premium Benefit is not payable if the policy has been assigned as collateral and the assignee has not released the assignment.

facts.name: Wellness Credit Definition
facts.sentence: Wellness Credit means a reduction in annual premium earned by satisfying qualifying health benchmarks under the BrightPath Vitality Program.

facts.name: Grace Period Definition
facts.sentence: Grace Period means the 31-day period after each premium due date during which this policy remains in force.

facts.name: ROP Benefit Void on Assignment
facts.sentence: The Return-of-Premium (ROP) benefit is not payable if the policy has been assigned as collateral.

facts.name: Assignee Release Required
facts.sentence: The assignee must release the assignment for the ROP benefit to become payable.

facts.name: Free Enrollment in Vitality Program
facts.sentence: The owner may enroll in the BrightPath Vitality Program at no additional cost.

facts.name: Annual Wellness Credit Calculation
facts.sentence: Wellness Credits are calculated annually on each policy anniversary.

facts.name: Wellness Credit Eligibility
facts.sentence: Wellness Credits are based on the insured's participation in qualifying activities.

facts.name: Annual Preventive Health Exam
facts.sentence: Qualifying activities include an annual preventive health examination.

facts.name: Annual Exam Wellness Credit
facts.sentence: An annual preventive health examination provides up to $120 per year in Wellness Credits.

facts.name: Fitness Activity Qualification
facts.sentence: Verified fitness activity of 150 minutes or more per week qualifies for Wellness Credits.

facts.name: Fitness Activity Wellness Credit
facts.sentence: Verified fitness activity of 150+ minutes per week provides up to $96 per year in Wellness Credits.

facts.name: Tobacco-Free Certification Eligibility
facts.sentence: Tobacco-free certification qualifies for Wellness Credits.

facts.name: Tobacco-Free Credit Benefit
facts.sentence: Tobacco-free certification provides up to $60 per year in Wellness Credits.

facts.name: Max Wellness Credit Limit
facts.sentence: Maximum annual Wellness Credit shall not exceed $276.

facts.name: Wellness Credit Cap
facts.sentence: Maximum annual Wellness Credit shall not exceed 20% of the annual base premium.

facts.name: Maximum Wellness Credit Cap
facts.sentence: The lesser amount between $276 and 20% of the annual base premium determines the maximum annual Wellness Credit.

facts.name: Premium Offset via Wellness Credits
facts.sentence: Wellness Credits are applied as a premium offset against the next policy year's premiums.

facts.name: No Cash Value Accumulation
facts.sentence: Wellness Credits do not accumulate cash value.

facts.name: Forfeiture of Unearned Credits
facts.sentence: Unearned Wellness Credits are forfeited if not earned.

facts.name: Right to Modify Activities
facts.sentence: BrightPath reserves the right to modify qualifying activities.

facts.name: Modifications Require 90-Day Notice
facts.sentence: Any modification to qualifying activities requires 90 days’ written notice to the policy owner.

facts.name: Monthly Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: Premiums are due on the first day of each month.

facts.name: Grace Period for Premium Payments
facts.sentence: A grace period of 31 days follows each premium due date.

facts.name: Grace Period Continuity
facts.sentence: Coverage remains uninterrupted during the grace period.

facts.name: Policy Lapse Due to Non-Payment
facts.sentence: Failure to pay premiums by the end of the grace period results in policy lapse.

facts.name: Policy Lapse Consequences
facts.sentence: Policy lapse terminates all benefits under the policy.

facts.name: ROP Benefit Termination on Lapse
facts.sentence: Accrued return-of-premium benefit is terminated upon policy lapse.

facts.name: Policy Reinstatement Window
facts.sentence: Reinstatement is available within three years of policy lapse.

facts.name: Reinstatement Insurability Requirement
facts.sentence: Evidence of insurability satisfactory to BrightPath is required for reinstatement.

facts.name: Reinstatement Interest Requirement
facts.sentence: Overdue premiums must be paid with 6% annual interest for reinstatement.

facts.name: Reinstatement Fee Requirement
facts.sentence: Applicable reinstatement fees must be paid for reinstatement.

facts.name: Suicide Clause Application
facts.sentence: The suicide clause applies if the insured dies by suicide, whether sane or insane.

facts.name: Suicide Clause Timing
facts.sentence: The suicide clause is effective within two years of the issue date.

facts.name: Suicide Clause Liability Limit
facts.sentence: If the suicide clause applies, BrightPath's total liability is limited to a refund of base premiums paid.

facts.name: Suicide Clause Refund Limit
facts.sentence: The refund of base premiums paid does not include interest.

facts.name: Aviation Death Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if death results from the insured acting as a pilot of any non-commercial aircraft.

facts.name: Aviation Co-Pilot Death Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if death results from the insured acting as a co-pilot of any non-commercial aircraft.

facts.name: Aviation Crew Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if death results from the insured acting as a crew member of any non-commercial aircraft.

facts.name: Aviation Exclusion Exception
facts.sentence: An aviation exclusion does not apply if the Aviation Rider is attached to the policy.

facts.name: No Additional Exclusions
facts.sentence: There are no other exclusions besides those specified in Section 9.

facts.name: Conversion Privilege
facts.sentence: The owner may convert all or part of the death benefit to any permanent life insurance plan offered by BrightPath.

facts.name: No Evidence of Insurability
facts.sentence: Conversion can occur without evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Conversion Timing Requirement
facts.sentence: Conversion must be requested at least 5 years before the policy maturity date.

facts.name: Conversion Age Limit
facts.sentence: The insured must not have yet reached age 60 to qualify for conversion.

facts.name: Minimum Convertible Amount
facts.sentence: The minimum convertible amount is $100,000.

facts.name: Partial Conversion Premium Adjustment
facts.sentence: Upon partial conversion, premiums under this policy will be proportionally reduced.

facts.name: Partial Conversion Adjustment
facts.sentence: After partial conversion, the ROP benefit will be adjusted to reflect premiums paid on the remaining term coverage only.

facts.name: Death Claim Submission Requirement
facts.sentence: To file a death claim, the beneficiary must submit Form BP-CLM-01.

facts.name: Death Claim Documentation Requirement
facts.sentence: To file a death claim, the beneficiary must submit a certified copy of the death certificate.

facts.name: Death Claim Submission Requirement
facts.sentence: To file a death claim, the beneficiary must submit the original policy document or a lost-policy affidavit.

facts.name: ROP Claim Requirement
facts.sentence: To claim the ROP benefit, the owner must submit Form BP-MAT-01.

facts.name: ROP Benefit Claim Requirement
facts.sentence: To claim the ROP benefit, the owner must submit photo identification.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: All claims must be submitted to BrightPath Life Insurance Corporation.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: Claims should be sent to the Policyholder Services — Claims department.

facts.name: Claims Mailing Address
facts.sentence: The mailing address for claims is 88 Commerce Drive, Suite 400, Columbus, OH 43215.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Valid claims will be paid within 30 days of receiving all required documentation.

facts.name: Policy Issuance Date
facts.sentence: BrightPath Life Insurance Corporation issued a policy on February 1, 2024.

facts.name: Service Address Location
facts.sentence: The address for service-related communications is 88 Commerce Drive, Suite 400, Columbus, OH 43215.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: BrightPath Life Insurance Corporation will pay valid claims within 30 days of receiving all required documentation.

facts.name: Incontestability Clause
facts.sentence: After a policy has been in force during the insured's lifetime for two years from the issue date, BrightPath Life Insurance Corporation may not contest the policy.

facts.name: Incontestability Exception
facts.sentence: The only exception to the incontestability provision is non-payment of premium.

facts.name: Misstatement of Age Adjustment
facts.sentence: If age is misstated on the policy, the death benefit will be adjusted to reflect the amount the premiums paid would have purchased at the correct age.

facts.name: Death Benefit Adjustment for Misstated Sex
facts.sentence: If sex is misstated on the policy, the death benefit will be adjusted to reflect the amount the premiums paid would have purchased at the correct sex.

facts.name: Entire Contract Clause
facts.sentence: This policy, together with the attached application, constitutes the entire contract between the parties.

facts.name: Oral Modification Prohibition
facts.sentence: No agent of BrightPath Life Insurance Corporation may modify this policy through oral agreement.

facts.name: Permitted Policy Assignments
facts.sentence: Absolute assignments of the policy are permitted by BrightPath Life Insurance Corporation.

facts.name: Permitted Collateral Assignments
facts.sentence: Collateral assignments of the policy are permitted by BrightPath Life Insurance Corporation.

facts.name: Assignment Notice Requirement
facts.sentence: Written notice to BrightPath Life Insurance Corporation’s home office is required before any assignment becomes binding on the company.

facts.sentence: The joint monthly premium is $142.00.

facts.name: Monthly Automatic Deduction
facts.sentence: Premium payments are made via monthly automatic deduction.

facts.name: Contingent Beneficiary Designation
facts.sentence: The contingent beneficiary under the insurance policy is the Reyes Family Irrevocable Trust.

facts.name: Trust Establishment Date
facts.sentence: The trust was established on March 1, 2024.

facts.name: Contingent Beneficiary Designation
facts.sentence: The Reyes Family Irrevocable Trust holds a 100% interest in the contingent beneficiary designation.

facts.name: First-to-Die Event Definition
facts.sentence: A 'First-to-Die Event' refers to the death of the insured person who dies first while the policy is in force.

facts.name: Surviving Insured Definition
facts.sentence: A 'Surviving Insured' is defined as the insured person who remains alive after the First-to-Die Event.

facts.name: Continuation Option Right
facts.sentence: The 'Continuation Option' grants the surviving insured the right to obtain a new individual policy as specified in Section 8.

facts.name: Grace Period Duration
facts.sentence: The 'Grace Period' lasts for 31 days following a missed premium due date.

facts.name: Grace Period Coverage Continuity
facts.sentence: During the Grace Period, coverage remains active despite a missed premium payment.

facts.name: Blended Age Pricing
facts.sentence: 'Joint Age' is the blended age used by Meridian Mutual to price joint policies.

facts.name: Joint Age Calculation Timing
facts.sentence: 'Joint Age' is calculated at the time of policy issuance.

facts.name: Pricing via Joint Age
facts.sentence: Meridian Mutual uses 'Joint Age' to determine pricing for joint life insurance policies.

facts.name: Death Benefit Trigger
facts.sentence: The death benefit will be paid upon the occurrence of a First-to-Die Event.

facts.name: Policy In Force Condition
facts.sentence: Payment of the death benefit requires that the policy be in force on the date of death.

facts.name: Death Before Expiry Condition
facts.sentence: Payment of the death benefit requires that the death occur before the policy expiry date.

facts.name: Proof of Death Requirement
facts.sentence: Satisfactory proof of death must be received by the insurer prior to death benefit disbursement.

facts.name: Policy Termination Post-Payout
facts.sentence: After the death benefit is paid, the policy terminates with respect to both insured individuals.

facts.name: Continuation Option Preserved
facts.sentence: Termination of the policy does not override the provisions outlined in Section 8 regarding the Continuation Option.

facts.name: Simultaneous Death Rule
facts.sentence: If both insured persons die simultaneously or within 24 hours of each other, the older insured is treated as having died first.

facts.name: Simultaneous Death Payout Rule
facts.sentence: When both insureds die within 24 hours of each other, the death benefit is payable to the contingent beneficiary.

facts.name: Lump Sum Death Benefit
facts.sentence: The death benefit will be paid in a lump sum amount.

facts.name: Death Benefit Disbursement Timeline
facts.sentence: The death benefit will be disbursed within 30 days of claim approval.

facts.name: Monthly Joint Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: A single joint premium is required monthly on the 10th day of each month.

facts.name: Grace Period Trigger
facts.sentence: Each missed premium due date triggers a 31-day Grace Period.

facts.name: Grace Period Payment Requirement
facts.sentence: Premium payments must be made within the Grace Period to maintain coverage.

facts.name: Policy Lapse Due to Non-Payment
facts.sentence: Failure to pay premiums after the end of the Grace Period results in lapse of the policy.

facts.name: Monthly Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: A single joint premium is due monthly on the 10th.

facts.name: Grace Period Duration
facts.sentence: A grace period of 31 days follows each missed due date.

facts.name: Policy Lapse After Grace Period
facts.sentence: If premiums remain unpaid after the grace period, the policy lapses.

facts.name: Policy Lapse Due to Nonpayment
facts.sentence: If premiums remain unpaid after the grace period, all coverage terminates.

facts.name: Joint Premium Responsibility
facts.sentence: Either joint owner may pay the premium.

facts.name: Joint Owner Payment Responsibility
facts.sentence: Payment by one joint owner satisfies the obligation of both joint owners.

facts.name: Suicide Clause Liability
facts.sentence: If either insured commits suicide within two years of the issue date, the insurer's liability is limited to a refund of premiums paid.

facts.name: Suicide Clause Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: If either insured commits suicide within two years of the issue date, no death benefit shall be payable.

facts.name: Suicide Clause Coverage
facts.sentence: Suicide includes cases where the insured is sane or insane.

facts.name: War Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the first-to-die event results directly from declared war.

facts.name: War Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the first-to-die event results indirectly from declared war.

facts.name: War Exclusion – Undeclared War
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the first-to-die event results directly from undeclared war.

facts.name: War Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the first-to-die event results indirectly from undeclared war.

facts.name: Death Benefit Exclusion: Armed Conflict
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the first-to-die event results directly from armed conflict.

facts.name: War Exclusion – Indirect Armed Conflict
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the first-to-die event results indirectly from armed conflict.

facts.name: Military Participation Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the first-to-die event results from the insured's participation in a military operation.

facts.name: Civilian Non-Combatant Exception
facts.sentence: A death benefit is payable if the insured was serving as a civilian non-combatant during a military operation.

facts.name: No Additional Exclusions
facts.sentence: No other exclusions apply besides those specified in Section 7.

facts.name: Continuation Option Eligibility
facts.sentence: Within 90 days of the first-to-die event, the surviving insured may elect to purchase a new individual level term life insurance policy from Meridian Mutual.

facts.name: Continuation Option Without Evidence
facts.sentence: The continuation option allows the surviving insured to purchase a new policy without providing evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Maximum Policy Face Amount Limit
facts.sentence: The new policy face amount may not exceed $1,000,000.

facts.name: Policy Term Limitation
facts.sentence: The new policy term may not exceed the remaining years on the original policy at the time of the first-to-die event.

facts.name: Premium Based on Attained Age
facts.sentence: The new premium will be based on the surviving insured's attained age.

facts.name: Premium Based on Current Rates
facts.sentence: The new premium will be based on then-current rate tables.

facts.name: Continuation Option Deadline
facts.sentence: The Continuation Option expires if not exercised within the 90-day window.

facts.name: Age Limitation on Continuation Option
facts.sentence: This option is not available if the surviving insured is age 65 or older at the time of the first-to-die event.

facts.name: Ownership & Divorce Rules
facts.sentence: Section 9 covers Ownership and Divorce Provision.

facts.name: Conversion Privilege Terms
facts.sentence: Section 10 covers Conversion Privilege.

facts.name: Claims Procedure
facts.sentence: Section 11 covers Claims Procedure.

facts.name: General Provisions Overview
facts.sentence: Section 12 covers General Provisions.

facts.name: Independent Ownership Rights
facts.sentence: Either joint owner may exercise ownership rights independently of the other.

facts.name: Beneficiary Change Rights
facts.sentence: Ownership rights include the ability to change beneficiaries.

facts.name: Ownership Severance Request
facts.sentence: Upon legal dissolution of the marriage or domestic partnership of the two insureds, either insured may request severance of ownership.

facts.name: Ownership Severance Requirements
facts.sentence: Severance of ownership requires a court decree or written mutual consent.

facts.name: Policy Split on Severance
facts.sentence: Meridian Mutual will split the policy into two individual policies of $500,000 each upon severance.

facts.name: Severance Ownership Transfer
facts.sentence: Alternatively, Meridian Mutual may assign sole ownership and continued coverage on the full amount to one insured.

facts.name: Ownership Release Condition
facts.sentence: The non-designated insured’s interest is released when sole ownership is assigned.

facts.name: Severance Request Deadline
facts.sentence: A severance request must be made before the earlier of the policy expiry date or the first-to-die event.

facts.name: Policy Conversion Before First-To-Die Event
facts.sentence: Prior to the first-to-die event, owners may convert the joint policy to two individual permanent life insurance policies.

facts.name: No Evidence of Insurability Required
facts.sentence: Conversion can occur without evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Conversion Deadline Conditions
facts.sentence: Conversion must occur before the earlier of the 15th policy anniversary or the younger insured's 60th birthday.

facts.name: Conversion Benefit Limit
facts.sentence: Each converted policy may cover up to 50% of the current death benefit.

facts.name: Submit Claim Form MM-CLM-10
facts.sentence: To file a claim, submit Form MM-CLM-10 to Meridian Mutual.

facts.name: Claim Filing Requirement
facts.sentence: A certified death certificate of the deceased insured must be submitted to file a claim.

facts.name: Claim Documentation Requirement
facts.sentence: An original policy document or a lost-policy affidavit must be submitted to file a claim.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: Claims should be sent to Meridian Mutual Life – Claims Administration at One Meridian Plaza, P.O. Box 8800, Minneapolis, MN 55402.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Valid claims are paid within 30 days of complete submission.

facts.name: Policy Number Confirmation
facts.sentence: Policy number MN 55402 exists.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Valid claims under the policy are paid within 30 days of complete submission.

facts.name: Policy Incontestability Clause
facts.sentence: This policy becomes incontestable after being in force for two years from the issue date.

facts.name: Incontestability Clause Duration
facts.sentence: The incontestability clause applies during the lifetime of either insured person.

facts.name: Post-two-year contestability limit
facts.sentence: The insurer may contest the policy only for non-payment of premium after two years.

facts.name: Age Misstatement Adjustment
facts.sentence: If the age of either insured is misstated, the benefit amount will be adjusted.

facts.name: Age Misstatement Adjustment Rule
facts.sentence: The adjustment for misstated age is based on the correct age of the insured.

facts.name: Benefit Adjustment for Misstated Sex
facts.sentence: If the sex of either insured is misstated, the benefit amount will be adjusted.

facts.name: Misstatement of Sex Adjustment
facts.sentence: The adjustment for misstated sex is based on the correct sex of the insured.

facts.name: Benefit Adjustment via Blended Age
facts.sentence: The benefit adjustment uses the blended joint age of both insured individuals.

facts.name: Entire Contract Clause
facts.sentence: The policy and the application form together constitute the entire agreement between parties.

facts.name: Governing Law – Minnesota
facts.sentence: This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Minnesota.

facts.name: Authorized Signature Role
facts.sentence: The authorized signature on the policy is held by a Senior Vice President, Underwriting.

facts.name: Employment Confirmation
facts.sentence: The individual signing is employed by Meridian Mutual Life.

facts.name: Policy Issuance by Meridian Mutual Life
facts.sentence: Meridian Mutual Life issued the policy.

facts.name: Policy Issue Date
facts.sentence: The policy was issued on March 10, 2024.

facts.sentence: This policy is payable to a business entity.

facts.name: Key Person Indemnification
facts.sentence: The purpose of this policy is key person indemnification.

facts.name: Death Benefit Definition
facts.sentence: The term 'Death Benefit' means the face amount payable upon the death of the insured while this policy is in force.

facts.name: Key Person Definition
facts.sentence: The term 'Key Person' means the insured individual whose skills, relationships, or knowledge are essential to the business operations of the policy owner.

facts.name: Annual Premium Due Date Definition
facts.sentence: The term 'Annual Premium Due Date' means April 5 of each policy year.

facts.name: Grace Period Definition
facts.sentence: The term 'Grace Period' means the 31-day period following the premium due date, during which coverage remains in force.

facts.name: Change in Insurable Interest Definition
facts.sentence: The term 'Change in Insurable Interest' means any event that causes the owner to no longer have an insurable interest in the insured's life, including termination of the insured's employment or ownership relationship.

facts.name: Death Benefit Eligibility Condition
facts.sentence: We will pay the death benefit to the named beneficiary if the insured dies while this policy is in force.

facts.name: Death Before Expiry Condition
facts.sentence: We will pay the death benefit to the named beneficiary if death occurs before the policy expiry date.

facts.name: Proof of Death Requirement
facts.sentence: We will pay the death benefit to the named beneficiary if we receive proof of death satisfactory to us.

facts.name: Lump Sum Payout Timing
facts.sentence: The death benefit is paid in a single lump sum within 30 days of approval of all required claim documents.

facts.name: Death Benefit Termination
facts.sentence: Payment of the death benefit terminates this policy.

facts.name: Insurable Interest at Issuance
facts.sentence: At policy issuance, a valid business insurable interest exists in the life of the insured by reason of the insured's role as a key officer or employee of the owner.

facts.name: Notification Requirement After Termination
facts.sentence: If the insured's employment or key-person relationship with the owner terminates for any reason, the owner must notify us within 60 days.

facts.name: Policy Transfer After Termination
facts.sentence: Upon notification of termination of employment or key-person relationship, the owner may assign this policy to the insured as new owner, subject to our written acknowledgment.

facts.name: Surrender After Termination
facts.sentence: Upon notification of termination of employment or key-person relationship, the owner may surrender this policy for no cash value.

facts.name: No Death Benefit Without Insurable Interest
facts.sentence: We will not pay the death benefit if, at the time of death, the owner no longer has an insurable interest in the insured’s life.

facts.name: Policy Transfer to Insured
facts.sentence: The policy can be transferred to the insured as the new owner.

facts.name: Ownership Transfer Requirement
facts.sentence: Ownership transfer requires the insurer’s written acknowledgment.

facts.name: Surrender Option Without Value
facts.sentence: An alternative to transferring ownership is surrendering the policy for no cash value.

facts.name: Ownership Continuity Requirement
facts.sentence: The insurer will not pay the death benefit if the owner does not employ or maintain an active business relationship with the insured at the time of death.

facts.name: Ownership Transfer Requirement
facts.sentence: The insurer will not pay the death benefit if the owner fails to transfer ownership per Section 6.3(a).

facts.name: Annual Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: The annual premium is due on April 5 of each policy year.

facts.name: Grace Period After Due Date
facts.sentence: A 31-day grace period follows each annual premium due date.

facts.name: Grace Period Coverage Continuity
facts.sentence: Coverage remains effective during the grace period.

facts.name: Policy Lapse Due to Non-Payment
facts.sentence: Failure to pay the premium by the end of the grace period causes the policy to lapse.

facts.name: Policy Lapse Without Value
facts.sentence: Lapse occurs with no cash value or return value.

facts.name: Policy Reinstatement Window
facts.sentence: Reinstatement may be requested within 2 years of lapse.

facts.name: Reinstatement Insurability Requirement
facts.sentence: Reinstatement requires satisfactory evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Reinstatement Requirements
facts.sentence: Reinstatement requires payment of all overdue premiums.

facts.name: Reinstatement Interest Requirement
facts.sentence: Reinstatement requires payment of 7% annual interest on overdue premiums.

facts.name: Suicide Within Two Years
facts.sentence: If the insured dies by suicide within two years of the issue date, the insurer’s liability is limited to a refund of premiums paid.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: If the insured dies by suicide within two years of the issue date, no death benefit is payable.

facts.name: Suicide Mental State Inclusion
facts.sentence: Suicide includes both sane and insane states of mind.

facts.name: Felony Death Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the insured's death results directly from the insured's commission of a felony.

facts.name: Felony Attempt Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the insured's death results directly from the insured's attempt to commit a felony.

facts.name: Felony Determination Requirement
facts.sentence: The determination of felony involvement must be made by a court of competent jurisdiction.

facts.name: Fraudulent Policy Acquisition
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if the policy was obtained through material misrepresentation by the policy owner.

facts.name: Fraud via Misrepresentation
facts.sentence: Material misrepresentation pertains to the nature of the insurable interest.

facts.name: Split-Dollar Endorsement Election
facts.sentence: The policy owner may elect to add a Split-Dollar Endorsement at policy issuance.

facts.name: Split-Dollar Endorsement Election
facts.sentence: The policy owner may elect to add a Split-Dollar Endorsement at any policy anniversary.

facts.name: Premium Sharing Arrangement
facts.sentence: Under the Split-Dollar Endorsement, premiums may be shared between the owner and the insured.

facts.name: Premium Sharing Agreement Requirement
facts.sentence: Premium sharing under the Split-Dollar Endorsement must occur pursuant to a written agreement.

facts.name: Split-Dollar Addition Timing
facts.sentence: A Split-Dollar Endorsement may be added to a policy at policy issuance.

facts.name: Split-Dollar Addition Timing
facts.sentence: A Split-Dollar Endorsement may be added to a policy on any policy anniversary.

facts.name: Premium Sharing Arrangement
facts.sentence: The Split-Dollar Endorsement allows premiums to be shared between the owner and the insured.

facts.name: Written Agreement Required
facts.sentence: Premium sharing under the Split-Dollar Endorsement requires a written split-dollar agreement.

facts.name: Death Benefit Allocation
facts.sentence: Under the Split-Dollar Endorsement, the death benefit may be split between the owner and a personal beneficiary.

facts.name: Loan Repayment Tranche Allocation
facts.sentence: The loan repayment tranche of the death benefit goes to the owner under the Split-Dollar Endorsement.

facts.name: Insured Designates Beneficiary
facts.sentence: The personal beneficiary who receives part of the death benefit under the Split-Dollar Endorsement is designated by the insured.

facts.name: Written Request Requirement
facts.sentence: The Split-Dollar Endorsement must be requested in writing.

facts.name: Endorsement Approval Requirement
facts.sentence: The Split-Dollar Endorsement is subject to Vanguard Sentinel’s then-current endorsement forms.

facts.name: IRS Tax Treatment of Split-Dollar Arrangements
facts.sentence: Tax treatment of split-dollar arrangements is governed by applicable IRS regulations.

facts.name: No Tax Representation Disclaimer
facts.sentence: Vanguard Sentinel makes no representations about the tax consequences of split-dollar arrangements.

facts.name: Policy Conversion Privilege
facts.sentence: The owner may convert this policy to a permanent life insurance plan offered by Vanguard Sentinel.

facts.name: No Insurability Requirement for Conversion
facts.sentence: Conversion to a permanent life insurance plan does not require evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Conversion Deadline Requirement
facts.sentence: The request for conversion must be made before the policy reaches its 8th anniversary.

facts.name: Conversion Age Limit
facts.sentence: The insured’s attained age must not exceed 65 at the time of conversion.

facts.name: Post-Conversion Ownership Options
facts.sentence: After conversion, the new policy owner may be the business entity.

facts.name: Post-Conversion Ownership Option
facts.sentence: After conversion, the new policy owner may be the insured personally.

facts.name: Ownership Documents Required for Conversion
facts.sentence: Execution of appropriate ownership documents is required when converting the policy.

facts.name: Claim Form Submission Requirement
facts.sentence: To file a claim, the policy owner must submit a completed claim form.

facts.name: Claim Form Requirement
facts.sentence: The required claim form is Form VS-BIZ-CLM.

facts.name: Claim Documentation Requirement
facts.sentence: To file a claim, a certified copy of the death certificate must be submitted.

facts.name: Insurable Interest Requirement
facts.sentence: Evidence of continued insurable interest at the time of death must be submitted to file a claim.

facts.name: Evidence of Insurable Interest Examples
facts.sentence: Examples of evidence of continued insurable interest include employment records or LLC records.

facts.name: Original Policy Submission Requirement
facts.sentence: An original policy must be submitted to file a claim.

facts.name: Lost Policy Claim Requirement
facts.sentence: If the original policy is lost, a lost-policy affidavit must be submitted to file a claim.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: Claims must be submitted to Vanguard Sentinel Life Insurance Company.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: Claims should be sent to the Corporate Claims Division of Vanguard Sentinel Life Insurance Company.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: The address for submitting claims is 500 Sentinel Tower, Suite 200, Cincinnati, OH 45202.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Valid claims will be paid within 30 days of receiving all required documentation.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Vanguard Sentinel Life Insurance Company will pay valid claims within 30 days of receiving all required documentation.

facts.name: Incontestability Clause
facts.sentence: After two years from the issue date, Vanguard Sentinel Life Insurance Company will not contest this policy on the basis of statements in the application.

facts.name: Post-two-year non-payment contestability
facts.sentence: Vanguard Sentinel Life Insurance Company may contest this policy on the basis of non-payment of premium after two years from the issue date.

facts.name: Post-Issue Contestability Limitation
facts.sentence: Vanguard Sentinel Life Insurance Company may contest this policy on the basis of lack of insurable interest after two years from the issue date.

facts.name: Age Misstatement Adjustment
facts.sentence: If age is misstated in the application, the death benefit will be adjusted to the amount purchasable at the correct age for the premium paid.

facts.name: Death Benefit Adjustment for Misstated Sex
facts.sentence: If sex is misstated in the application, the death benefit will be adjusted to the amount purchasable at the correct sex for the premium paid.

facts.name: Entire Agreement Clause
facts.sentence: This policy and the attached application together constitute the entire agreement between the parties.

facts.name: Governing Law Jurisdiction
facts.sentence: This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Ohio.

facts.name: Authorized Signatory Role
facts.sentence: The authorized signature on this policy is that of the Vice President, Group & Business Markets of Vanguard Sentinel Life Insurance Company.

facts.sentence: The date issued for this policy is April 5, 2024.
